Reimagining NYC — Congestion Pricing Data Investigation

Winner of the Macaulay Honors College Datathon, with a team of three. We followed traffic and PM2.5 outward from the toll zone using MTA, Port Authority, NYC DOT, EPA and NYC Health data. My role: team lead. I verified the datasets and built the geospatial maps.

Macaulay Datathon finals · Oct 10, 2026
The Engineering Part

15+ government sources pulled live through public APIs, each cross-checked against a second source where one existed. NYC DOT's traffic counters rotate locations, so year-over-year totals compared different streets until segment, date, hour and direction were matched. Two traffic feeds weren't measuring the same thing: a unit mismatch inflated one by roughly double, and 2026 looked like a collapse until they were aligned.

What It Found

Inside the toll zone the numbers improved. Outside it, traffic rose at all three Bronx-connecting crossings, and PM2.5 rose beside one of them. The project shows timing and pattern, not proof of cause, and says so on the page.

02

NeuroRoute — Hazard-Aware Emergency Routing

Standard routing treats every emergency the same. NeuroRoute ranks 340 NYC destinations (145 hospitals and 195 police stations) around 44 hazard zones, and weights a cardiac case differently from a stroke, trauma, child or general emergency. A Flask and React.js app, deployed live on PythonAnywhere. Built for the CSC 331H honors course, April to May 2026, with me as team lead.

CSC 331H Honors · Apr–May 2026FlaskPythonReact.jsLeaflet.jsOpenStreetMapPythonAnywhere
Child Emergency → Specialist Hospital Routing
Emergency → Nearest Police Station
Engineering Approach

Each destination is scored per query on five factors: distance, ETA, service-type match, location risk and hazard exposure. The scores are normalised and combined in a weighted sum, with separate weights per emergency category. Everything is recomputed against live inputs on every request instead of from a precomputed graph.

Tradeoffs

The weights are set heuristically, since there is no labeled outcome data and a learned model would have been false precision. Per-query recomputation is cheap at 340 destinations; past a few thousand I'd move to precomputed distance matrices or a spatial index.

⌥ GitHub

03

SpotB&B — A Marketplace for Private Parking

Hosts list a driveway or garage space with the largest vehicle it fits and when it's open. Drivers search by destination, time and vehicle size and book it. The address stays hidden until a reservation is confirmed. Built with a team of five for Tech Talent Pipeline Capstone III (the app's interface is branded ParkNGo). My part: the seed data (real photos matched to each listing type, across all five boroughs) and the driver dashboard. I paired with a teammate on the same tasks to move faster, and they merged our shared code into the main branch.

List a spot · price, availability, vehicle fit
How It Works

One account, two roles: anyone can drive and host. Hosts publish a listing and manage it from a dashboard that also shows incoming bookings. Drivers get matching spots as cards and map markers that refresh as they pan and zoom, sorted by distance or price. Seed data covers all five boroughs, so the demo never opens on an empty screen.

Decisions the Team Made

Privacy is enforced on the server: exact coordinates are stored apart from rounded public ones, and the street address reaches only the owner and drivers with a confirmed reservation. Prices are calculated in 30-minute blocks on the server and recomputed at booking. The listing row is locked inside a database transaction while overlaps are checked, which prevents double-booking. Passwords are hashed with bcrypt and the session lives in an HTTP-only cookie.
